notes: Method. Sections were resolved with I.lookup("va", ref), and every quote was copied from I.text_of. A builder script then checked each quote against the section text after whitespace and quote-mark normalisation. Quotes checked: 230 against the index, 65 against official pages (VAC and local). Each quote is one sentence or clause, copied word for word, including the index's spacing before punctuation after cross-references (for example "§ 58.1-3916 .").

Not in the index: Va. Code §§ 58.1-3211 (tax relief restrictions) and 58.1-3229 (land use legislative intent) are cited without quotes. Also missing were §§ 20-14.2, 20-14.3, 64.2-1000, 62.1-44.15:36, :44, :45, :47 and :61, which were checked but not needed.

Versions. The index marks §§ 15.2-2201, 15.2-2286, 19.2-354, 24.2-709 and 24.2-709.1 "effective until January 1, 2027" and holds no successor text, and § 24.2-418 has a contingent 2026 amendment. Re-check these on or after January 1, 2027.

Albemarle and Staunton. Both sites refused the research client (HTTP 403 even for robots.txt). That refusal was respected: no disguised client was used, and no third-party copy of their pages was quoted. Their courts are verified on vacourts.gov. Their other offices are named by their role in state law and marked "not read".

Albemarle form of government. The file assumes, from general knowledge, that Albemarle uses the county executive form. Under it a director of finance holds the commissioner-of-the-revenue and treasurer powers (Va. Code §§ 15.2-519, 15.2-521, 15.2-522, 58.1-3123(A)) and the board of supervisors appoints the board of equalization (§ 58.1-3371). Verify this before relying on any Albemarle tax step.

Staunton cross-reference. A separate file written in the same run, fixtures/places/va/discovery-staunton.json, records Staunton office pages. Another agent read them in a desktop browser after the same 403, and that file's own notes describe this as a departure from the run's User-Agent rule. Nothing here relies on it. Its URLs could fill the Staunton "not read" office slots once that method is accepted.

Courts. Charlottesville and Albemarle share the 16th Judicial Circuit and District but keep separate circuit courts, general district courts and clerks, all in Charlottesville. Staunton is in the 25th Circuit and District. Which court applies depends on the residence of the person or the location of the land.

Privacy. Only offices and official pages are recorded. The court pages and city pages name clerks, judges, the registrar and staff, and the assessor page publishes a staff mailbox; none of these is recorded. Office mailboxes on city pages were also left out, because the office page URL is enough.

Stale local pages found. Charlottesville's Register to Vote page gives a 21-day registration deadline (state law now closes the books 10 days before). The city circuit court and general district court pages state older civil amount limits than Va. Code § 16.1-77 as indexed. Both are recorded in "observed" with their quotes.

Ladders. Escalation steps reuse the body refs of fixtures/authority/ladders.json (va.commissioner_revenue, va.tax_commissioner, va.circuit_court, va.gdc_or_circuit, va.foia_council, va.court_of_appeals) and name the matching rungs (va.business.4-7, va.records.5 and 7). Steps marked "inferred" have no statute that names the route.

Forms. fixtures/forms/forms.json supplies va-foia-request-letter and va-dc-495 (FOIA) and va-dc-211 (payment agreement for fines and costs). Charlottesville's GDC page refers to form DC-210, which is not in forms.json.

Scope left out: food establishment and septic permits (the state health department's local health districts), protective orders (the juvenile and domestic relations courts), and building rental inspection districts (Va. Code § 36-105.1:1). These are candidates for a next pass.
